data.title: Suntex Enterprises Retires 50 Million Common Shares and Announces Planned 25% Reduction in Authorized Shares
data.description:
Completed retirement reduces outstanding common shares by 6.48%, reinforcing capital discipline alongside the Company's development and operating priorities.

AUSTIN, TX / ACCESS Newswire / September 25, 2026 / Suntex Enterprises, Inc. ("Suntex" or the "Company") today announced the completed retirement of 50 million common shares, reducing its outstanding common shares from 771,550,223 to 721,550,223. The Company also announced plans to reduce its authorized common shares by 25%, from 1 billion to 750 million, subject to completion of the necessary corporate actions and filings.

These initiatives reflect Suntex's commitment to disciplined capital management as it advances its real estate development, construction and infrastructure businesses. The completed retirement reduces outstanding common shares by approximately 6.48%, while the planned authorized share reduction would lower the ceiling for future common share issuance by 250 million shares.

"Our responsibility is to grow the business while protecting the interests of the shareholders who own it," said Javier Leal, Chief Executive Officer of Suntex Enterprises. "Retiring 50 million shares and pursuing a lower authorized share ceiling put that responsibility into practice. As we advance our developments in Texas and Canada, we will evaluate capital decisions with the same discipline we apply to our projects: the economics must support the long-term interests of the Company and its shareholders."

Strengthening the Capital Structure

The completed retirement increases the proportional common equity ownership of shareholders whose holdings remain unchanged. Each retained common share now represents a larger percentage of Suntex's outstanding common stock.

The planned reduction in authorized common shares would establish a tighter framework for future common equity issuance. Together, these actions address both the Company's existing outstanding share count and its authorized capacity for additional issuance.

Suntex will confirm completion of the authorized share reduction once the required corporate actions and filings become effective.

Aligning Capital With Operating Priorities

Suntex's primary focus remains advancing its development initiatives in Texas and Canada while strengthening the capacity and performance of its construction and infrastructure businesses. Management's priorities include executing contracted work, progressing development milestones and allocating resources to opportunities supported by sound project economics.

The Company views capital structure discipline as an integral part of this strategy. Management intends to assess future uses of equity against their expected contribution to operating performance, asset growth and long-term shareholder value.

"We are building Suntex with a clear set of priorities: deliver our projects, strengthen our operating companies and earn an appropriate return on the capital we commit," Leal added. "Shareholders should be able to measure our progress through completed actions and business results. This retirement is one of those completed actions, and we intend to bring that same accountability to the next stage of growth."

About Suntex Enterprises, Inc.

Suntex Enterprises, Inc. focuses on real estate development, construction and infrastructure through its operating subsidiaries and development initiatives in the United States and Canada. The Company's strategy centers on expanding its operating businesses, developing its asset base and creating long-term shareholder value.

Disclaimer

Forward-Looking Statements

This press release contains forward-looking statements regarding the planned reduction in authorized common shares, development initiatives, operating expansion, capital allocation and shareholder value objectives. These statements reflect management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties, including completion of necessary corporate actions and filings, financing availability, project approvals, construction costs, execution risks and market conditions. Actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied. The Company undertakes no obligation to update forward-looking statements except as required by law.

data.title: Ather Energy to push for more exports
data.description:
Electric two-wheeler major Ather Energy on Friday said it will push for more exports by looking at countries in Asia and Latin America, for meaningful contribution to its revenues over the next five to seven years.

Having said that, the company also added that it will prioritise the domestic market amid the current demand-supply situation, as the current plant in Tamil Nadu (Hosur) is not sufficient to meet the demand. The company has started exporting to Nepal and Sri Lanka recently.

Speaking to businessline on the sidelines of a launch here, Ravneet S Phokela, Chief Business Officer, Ather Energy, said that Ather will add another 10 lakh units per annum at its upcoming facility in Maharashtra, which will be in two phases.

“So, our next pump up will come from our new facility, which is coming up in Maharashtra. That plant has a total capacity of 10-lakh more units, which is split in two phases — 5-lakh in the first phase and another in 5-lakh in the second phase. The first phase goes live around December this year, but typically it will take about four to six months for it to get to its full capacity,” he told businessline.

He said the company has a production capacity of around 30,000-35,000 units a month right now from the current plant, and from December, it is expecting to do around 42,000 units a month from both the facilities.

Meanwhile, the company launched its new electric scooter, Konarc, for the Delhi-NCR market, priced at ₹79,999. Phokela said Delhi-NCR continues to be an important market for Ather, with EV adoption increasing from 6.27 per cent in Q1 FY26 to 9.23 per cent in Q1 FY27, recording 38 per cent y-o-y growth.

data.title: Trump Calls Xi Meeting 'Very Productive.' What Investors Might Not Like. — Barrons.com
data.description:
Reshma Kapadia

President Donald Trump said in a social media post Friday he had a "very productive" meeting with Chinese leader Xi Jinping, but offered few details.

Trade Representative Jamieson Greer in a television interview Friday said details of what the two sides reached on trade would come Monday.

While investors likely will be pleased to see signs of a fragile peace between the two economic superpowers, the lack of deals and a shorter-than-expected extension of the rivals' latest truce leaves plenty of uncertainty for markets in the months ahead.

In fact, the biggest takeaway for investors so far actually happened before the summit. The two countries extended their truce that was set to expire on Nov. 10 for another two months-the brief extension underscores the distrust and frictions simmering beneath the friendly tone that the leaders struck.

"I had been pretty sanguine on the U.S.-China relationship. But with an extension of only two months, that's a bit concerning," says Rory Green, head of China research for TS Lombard.

Greer told CNBC on Friday that the two sides had made fresh progress in negotiations around U.S. agricultural products, medical devices, and Chinese consumer goods deemed nonsensitive, with more information coming next week. The U.S. and China have been discussing a Board of Trade that would lower tariffs on $30 billion of nonstrategic goods, with analysts expecting many of them to be consumer-oriented.

Otherwise, the much-anticipated summit between the leaders of the world's two largest economies brought a lot of optics, but not much substance. Xi's first visit to Washington, D.C. in a decade was heavy on ceremony and goodwill-building: Trump greeted him on the tarmac in a rare move, hosted him for a state dinner, and said they have "never gotten along better." Xi has been pushing to be recognized as a global power on par with the U.S., something the visit reinforced.

Both leaders talked up their strong rapport and vowed increased cooperation and communication as they try to navigate their geopolitical rivalry. The two leaders are intent on preserving stability to buy each country time to reduce their dependence on the other-and to forestall a series of retaliatory measures that would make both economies' domestic problems worse.

China's economy is still stuck in a multi-year rout, with another batch of data showing weakness, even as Xi tries to project strength and equal standing with the U.S. on the global stage. Trump has his own problems, including the Iran war stretching into its seventh month and rising prices ahead of midterm elections.

The talks, however, did little to address the biggest issues among the rivals. Among them are China's support for Iran and increased military posture in Asia, the continued trade imbalance between the U.S. and China, and the two countries' race to develop artificial intelligence. Instead, the short truce extension underscores the U.S. concerns about its access to rare-earth minerals and a desire to keep China to its commitments.

Write to Reshma Kapadia at reshma.kapadia@barrons.com

data.title: Wall St edges up on AI enthusiasm, Mideast negotiation hopes
data.description:
Key points:
  • Indexes up: Dow 0.34%, S&P 0.18%, Nasdaq 0.21%
  • Akamai Technologies surges on $11.6 billion Anthropic deal
  • Microsoft revamps Copilot with code generation, agentic AI tools
  • Core capital goods orders point to robust growth in August

By Johann M Cherian and Avinash P

Wall Street's main indexes inched higher in choppy trading on Friday as AI optimism buoyed sentiment and oil prices eased, while investors monitored efforts to secure a deal to end the Middle East conflict.

Microsoft shares rose 3.3% and were the biggest boost to the S&P 500, after the software giant unveiled several new capabilities in its Copilot app, including a coding tool and an always-on AI agent.

Chip maker Qualcomm gained 5.1% and Nvidia was marginally higher, while Dell advanced 5%.

AI-related optimism was a key driver this week, aided by Meta's Muse and its integrated device, Charm, gaining traction among young consumers. Some analysts pointed to it as a product of massive spending on the technology. However, the stock eased 3.2% and trimmed weekly gains to about 13%.

"The amount of money being deployed into the economy from AI investment is just so strong, and we haven't even seen the productivity piece of it," said Jamie Cox, managing partner at Harris Financial Group. "There's a little bit of that the market is weighing into the valuation and that's one of the reasons why you really can't get much of a selloff."

At 11:28 a.m. ET the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 176.76 points, or 0.34%, to 51,526.74, the S&P 500 gained 14.02 points, or 0.18%, to 7,718.15 and the Nasdaq Composite gained 57.69 points, or 0.21%, to 26,997.07.

Declines in seven of the 11 S&P 500 sectors were offset by a 0.8% gain in the heavyweight technology sector — the week's best performer. Both the S&P 500 and the tech-heavy Nasdaq were set for weekly advances.

A report that US and Iranian negotiators continued to explore a phased path out of the war, which would involve Tehran reopening the Strait of Hormuz and Washington lifting its economic blockade, helped market sentiment.

Data also showed strong AI capex boosted demand for key manufactured capital goods, outpacing expectations in August.

Optimism, however, was capped by inflation worries driven by prolonged Iran and Ukraine conflicts and soaring government debt. Brent crude eased early, but was still over $100 a barrel, while the yield on the 10-year Treasury note was at 5.2%.

Against this backdrop, traders see a 66.4% chance of the Federal Reserve increasing interest rates by at least 25 basis points in October, up from around 50% earlier this week, the CME Group's FedWatch Tool showed. Remarks from policymakers, including John Williams and Beth Hammack, are expected later in the day.

President Donald Trump said he had a "very productive meeting" with President Xi Jinping. Trump made it clear to Xi that Chinese help for Iran was unacceptable, said the US ambassador to China.

Akamai Technologies surged 7.3% after an $11.6 billion cloud services deal with AI leader Anthropic. People jumped 9% after a report said MGM Resorts International was discussing a bid for the online services company.

Declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 1.1-to-1 ratio on the NYSE and by a 1.06-to-1 ratio on the Nasdaq. The S&P 500 posted three new 52-week highs and 30 new lows while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 34 new highs and 123 new lows.

data.title: HDFC Mutual Fund Unveils Indian Sign Language Platform for Financial Literacy
data.description:
To commemorate the platform’s launch, HDFC Mutual Fund has also released a digital film that follows a young expecting couple from the Deaf and Hard of Hearing community as they imagine the future they want to build for their child

On the International Day of Sign Languages, HDFC Mutual Fund has launched a dedicated digital platform built entirely in Indian Sign Language (ISL) under its ongoing financial literacy initiative, Bharosa, designed for the Deaf and Hard of Hearing (DHH) community With this launch, HDFC Mutual Fund becomes the first Indian Asset Management Company (AMC) to build a platform of this kind, extending the idea of financial inclusion through accessible, sign language-based investor education and awareness initiative.

Launched in August 2025, Bharosa has already engaged around 6000 individuals from the DHH community through ISL‑based investor awareness sessions. It lets users choose a financial goal such as retirement or a child’s education and learn through curated ISL videos on that goal. Users can also schedule a one-on-one session with a DHH coach, who guides them through their financial journey in ISL.

Over the past year, HDFC Mutual Fund has engaged with the DHH community to understand how it navigates financial decisions. That engagement surfaced one concern repeatedly: the fear of being misled, not from a lack of ambition, but from a lack of information in a language people could fully understand. The finding gave the platform its name, ‘Bharosa’, meaning trust.

Speaking about the initiative, Navneet Munot, Managing Director & Chief Executive Officer, HDFC Asset Management Company, said, “Over the years financial inclusion has been measured by access to financial products and services. However, access alone is not enough. People also need information in a form they can follow before they can weigh their choices with any confidence.

Through our engagement with the Deaf and hard of hearing community, we learnt how rarely that information is offered in a language they use. Bharosa, our financial literacy platform built entirely in Indian Sign Language, is a step in that direction. It offers videos organised around the goals people save for and one-on-one sessions with coaches from within the community, so that more people can take well-informed financial decisions.”

To commemorate the platform’s launch, HDFC Mutual Fund has also released a digital film that follows a young expecting couple from the Deaf and Hard of Hearing community as they imagine the future they want to build for their child. In that exchange, a quiet, familiar uncertainty surfaces. The film shows how clarity about one's options can turn that uncertainty into confidence, right at the moments that matter most.

The actors featured in the film are members of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing community, bringing authenticity and true representation to the narrative. At its core, Bharosa is built on a simple belief: everyone deserves access to financial education in a language they understand. By making financial learning available through Indian Sign Language and a dedicated digital platform, HDFC Mutual Fund hopes to encourage a larger conversation around accessibility, inclusion and financial empowerment.

data.title: Embassy Reit Raises Rs 1,000 Cr From European Bank In First Trust-Level Bank Financing
data.description:
The three-year floating-rate debt will refinance existing borrowings as RBI’s June framework expands institutional funding options for Indian REITs

Bengaluru-based Embassy Real Estate Investment Trust (REIT) has raised Rs 1,000 crore through the issuance of non-convertible debentures (NCDs) to a scheduled European multinational bank. The proceeds will be used to refinance the trust’s existing debt.

The three-year floating-rate NCDs carry an initial coupon of 6.97 per cent and have been issued as Series XVIII debentures. The securities have received a AAA/Stable credit rating from CARE Ratings, according to an exchange filing by the trust on Friday.

The transaction marks the first financing by a scheduled commercial bank to an Indian REIT at the trust level. It follows the Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) framework introduced in June 2026, which allowed commercial banks to directly finance REITs.

Before the regulatory change, banks were restricted from lending directly to REITs at the trust level. REITs instead accessed debt financing through special purpose vehicles (SPVs), while also relying on bond issuances and equity markets to meet their funding requirements.

Highlighting the impact of the regulatory changes, Embassy REIT CEO Amit Shetty said, “Continued regulatory support from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) and RBI has strengthened access to long-term funding for REITs.”

Refinancing Existing Debt

The latest fundraising follows Embassy REIT’s Rs 1,400 crore NCD issuance in March 2026. The earlier issuance was aimed at strengthening the trust’s long-term capital base, with institutional investors continuing to show interest in large office assets.

The latest transaction is focused on refinancing existing debt, giving the trust another route to manage its borrowing requirements. Direct bank financing could also broaden funding options for REITs as they manage debt maturities and long-term capital requirements.

Embassy REIT currently owns and operates more than 52 million square feet (msf) of office space across Bengaluru, Mumbai, Pune, Delhi-National Capital Region (NCR) and Chennai. Its portfolio is spread across some of India’s major commercial real estate markets.

The financing comes after the RBI opened the door for direct bank lending to REITs at the trust level. The latest transaction adds bank funding to the existing mix of bonds, equity and SPV-level borrowing available to Indian REITs.

data.title: Govt Disburses Rs 36,754 Cr Incentives Under PLI Schemes Till June
data.description:
As of June 30, PLI beneficiaries had recorded production and sales worth Rs 23.79 lakh crore and exports of Rs 15.53 lakh crore

Government has disbursed Rs 36,754 crore in incentives to companies under its Production Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes as of June 30, with the programme attracting Rs 2.58 lakh crore in investment and driving a sharp expansion in production and exports, the commerce and industry ministry said on Friday.

The figures underline the scale of the government’s manufacturing push since the PLI programme was launched in 2020 across 14 sectors, with an approved outlay of Rs 1.91 lakh crore. The schemes were designed to attract investment, boost domestic manufacturing, increase exports, create jobs and reduce reliance on imports.

As of June 30, PLI beneficiaries had recorded production and sales worth Rs 23.79 lakh crore and exports of Rs 15.53 lakh crore, according to data released by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT).

The schemes have also generated more than 14.57 lakh direct and indirect jobs, the ministry said.

The latest figures show continued growth from the Rs 2.40 lakh crore of investment and more than Rs 14.15 lakh crore in employment-related gains reported by the government as of March 31.

Pharmaceutical manufacturing has been among the areas where the scheme has driven deeper localisation. The sector has recorded cumulative sales of more than Rs 3.64 lakh crore, while 1,931 pharmaceutical products have begun being manufactured domestically, including 191 bulk drugs produced in India for the first time, the ministry said.

In medical devices, technology-transfer projects involving global companies such as Siemens, Wipro GE and Philips have helped enable domestic production of CT and MRI systems, cath labs and ultrasound equipment.

PLI beneficiaries in the medical devices segment have generated Rs 6,475 crore in domestic sales, Rs 560 crore in exports and Rs 1,400 crore in revenue from implants, according to the ministry.

Electronics manufacturing has also expanded under the programme, with companies including Dell, HP, Lenovo, Acer, ASUS and HPE setting up domestic production either directly or through Indian electronics manufacturing services partners.

The government said PLI-supported companies are now manufacturing products including AI servers, solid-state drives, memory modules, power adapters, battery packs and display panels, indicating greater localisation of electronics supply chains.

In speciality steel, companies including JSW, Jindal Odisha, Tata Steel and AMNS have invested more than Rs 19,000 crore under the scheme. The investments are aimed at increasing domestic production of higher-value steel used in automobiles, defence, capital goods and renewable energy, while reducing imports.

The government launched the PLI programme to move beyond traditional manufacturing incentives by linking payouts to incremental production and sales. The 14-sector programme covers areas ranging from electronics and pharmaceuticals to automobiles, solar modules, speciality steel and textiles.

The data also comes as individual PLI programmes show varying levels of progress. For example, the automobile and auto-components scheme had attracted Rs 44,326 crore of investment by March 31, against its targeted investment of Rs 42,500 crore through March 2027.

data.title: Nifty Extends Losing Streak To 7 Weeks
data.description:
The seven-week slide marks the first such losing streak for the benchmark indices since the Covid-19 pandemic period

Indian equity markets recovered on 25 September, with the Nifty reclaiming the 23,100-mark and the Sensex gaining more than 300 points, but the rebound was not enough to prevent the benchmark indices from extending their losing streak to seven consecutive weeks.

The Sensex closed 315 points, or 0.43 per cent, higher at 73,896, while the Nifty gained 77 points, or 0.33 per cent, to end at 23,141. The Nifty Bank rose 142 points to 55,580, while the Nifty Midcap index declined 84 points to 60,906.

The seven-week slide marks the first such losing streak for the benchmark indices since the Covid-19 pandemic period. The Nifty fell around 1 per cent this week, taking its cumulative decline over the seven-week period to nearly 6 per cent. The Sensex fell 0.6 per cent during the week, while the Nifty Bank and Nifty Midcap indices declined around 2 per cent each.

Friday's recovery was led by select financial and automobile stocks. Axis Bank and Bajaj Finance were among the top Nifty gainers, while HDFC Bank rose 1 per cent amid expectations of an announcement on its next chief executive officer.

Most automobile stocks also recovered, with Mahindra & Mahindra rising 2 per cent to emerge as one of the day's strongest performers.

Banking stocks remained active amid developments around lenders. IDBI Bank gained 2 per cent after reports that the government was evaluating revised bids, while Jana Small Finance Bank rose amid expectations of a potential deal announcement. Federal Bank, however, declined.

The broader market failed to match the benchmark recovery. Market breadth was only mildly positive, with the advance-decline ratio at 5:4, while the Nifty Midcap index ended lower.

Hospital stocks remained under pressure, with Max Healthcare Institute and Fortis Healthcare declining 3-5 per cent. PB Fintech fell 4 per cent, extending its losses from the previous session, while TurtleMint dropped 20 per cent.

Multi Commodity Exchange of India (MCX) declined 3 per cent as investors booked profits after the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) approved foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) for trading in non-agricultural commodity derivatives.

Among mid-cap stocks, Kaynes Technology, Supreme Industries, Indian Renewable Energy Development Agency (Ireda), Blue Star and Manappuram Finance were among the notable gainers.

The weekly performance remained broadly weak across the market. Information technology (IT) stocks were the biggest sectoral laggards, with the sectoral index falling 2 per cent, while fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) was the only major sectoral pocket to post a stronger performance, gaining 1 per cent over the week.

data.title: Zelio E-Mobility Plans To Raise Rs 168 Cr Via Preferential Issue
data.description:
Zelio E-Mobility, an electric two and three-wheeler manufacturer, has received board approval (subject to the approval of the shareholders, the in-principle approval of BSE Limited and other statutory / regulatory approvals) to raise up to 167.96 crore through a preferential issue of equity shares and convertible warrants. The proposed fundraise is aimed primarily at supporting the company’s next phase of expansion across India.

The BSE SME listed company proposes to issue up to 9.73 lakh equity shares at Rs 853 per share to four non promoter institutional and private investors, aggregating nearly Rs 83 crores.

The allottees include Motilal Oswal Financial Services at Rs 40.1 crore, Calliope Capital Advisors LLP owned by Navin Agarwal at Rs 31.4 crore, Param Value Investments, owned and controlled by veteran Indian equity investor Mukul Agrawal at Rs 8.5 crore and Hem Growth Opportunities Fund at nearly Rs 3 crore.

Simultaneously, the board approved the issue of up to 9.96 lakh convertible warrants at Rs 853 each to promoters Niraj Arya, Deepak Arya and Kunal Arya, aggregating nearly Rs 85 crores, with 25 per cent of the issue price payable upfront and the balance 75 per cent payable at the time of conversion, within 18 months from allotment.

Given the issue size, SEBI registered Brickwork Ratings India has been appointed to monitor utilisation of the proceeds.

The proposed fundraise also comes as Zelio continues to strengthen its investor base, with Motilal Oswal Financial Services and investor Mukul Agrawal having been key investors in the company.

The company has simultaneously been expanding its manufacturing footprint, with three plants now operational across Haryana, Tamil Nadu and Odisha. Its Ladwa facility in Haryana spans 2,63,450 sq. ft., while the Coimbatore facility covers approximately 39,000 sq. ft. and the Cuttack facility approximately 30,500 sq. ft. Zelio is also developing a new three-wheeler manufacturing plant in Patan, Haryana, with the proposed capital expected to support its development and wider expansion across India.

Commenting on the development, Kunal Arya, Managing Director, Zelio E-Mobility, said, “Our next phase is about building the capacity and market reach needed to serve a much larger customer base across India. The proposed fundraise will give us greater room to expand our manufacturing footprint, strengthen our distribution network and accelerate the development of our upcoming three-wheeler facility in Patan. We have built the business with a focus on profitable growth, and the priority now is to take that foundation into more markets while continuing to invest in the capabilities needed for scale.”

The proposed fundraise follows a strong financial growth trajectory. Zelio’s revenue increased 76.28 per cent year on year to Rs 303.54 crore (standalone revenue from operations) in FY2025–26, while its revenue CAGR stood at 121 per cent over the last four years. The company has remained profitable since inception. It was listed on the BSE SME in October 2025 at an issue price of Rs 136 per share, through which it raised Rs 62.83 crore through a fresh issue (the total IPO size being Rs 78.34 crore, including an offer for sale of Rs 15.50 crore), and has since seen significant movement in its stock with current price of Rs 1,036.20.

The company currently has a network of more than 400 dealers across 25+ states and is targeting 550+ dealerships by FY27. The planned expansion is intended to deepen its presence across existing markets while opening up additional markets for its electric two and three-wheeler portfolio.

Zelio will seek shareholder approval for the proposed preferential issue at an Extraordinary General Meeting scheduled for October 20, 2026. Shareholders will also consider proposed related party transactions of up to Rs 50 crore each with Torque Innovation EV, AVR Auto Industries, Jai Bharat Engineering Tools, Jai Bharat Auto Components and Rajdhani Machinery Store. The preferential issue is also subject to the in-principle approval of BSE Limited and other statutory / regulatory approvals as may be required.

data.title: Starbucks Expands Chennai GCC As North America Restructuring Continues
data.description:
The coffee chain plans to create around 800 technology roles in Chennai while cutting stores and corporate positions across North America

Starbucks is expanding its technology footprint in India even as it continues a restructuring programme across North America involving store closures, workforce reductions and cost-cutting measures under Chief Executive Brian Niccol.

The US-based coffee chain recently announced plans to establish its first Global Capability Centre (GCC) in India, while separately confirming plans to close around 250 underperforming stores across North America. The contrasting moves reflect Starbucks’ focus on building technology and business capabilities while streamlining its retail and corporate operations.

Chennai Centre To Create Jobs

Starbucks has signed a Memorandum of Understanding with Guidance Tamil Nadu to establish its first GCC in Chennai. The facility is expected to create high-skilled employment opportunities for approximately 800 technology professionals and support technology development and business solutions for Starbucks globally.

The GCC will operate independently of Tata Consumer Products, Starbucks’ retail joint venture partner in India. The Tamil Nadu government has positioned the project as part of its efforts to attract high-value GCC investments and create skilled employment opportunities.

Anand Varadarajan, Chief Technology Officer, Starbucks, cited Chennai’s technology talent pool, relatively low attrition levels, infrastructure and government support among the factors behind the decision. The investment value of the project has not been disclosed by the government.

North America Store Closures

At the same time, Starbucks is reducing parts of its North American retail footprint. According to The Wall Street Journal, the company plans to close approximately 250 low-performing cafes across North America, with around US$300 million in restructuring charges expected to be associated with the closures.

The latest store reductions represent the second major round of closures since Niccol became chief executive in September 2024.

Starbucks Chief Operating Officer Mike Grams said in a message to employees cited by The Wall Street Journal that some stores continued to underperform despite employee efforts. The company plans to transfer baristas where possible and provide severance support to affected employees who leave the organisation.

Corporate Workforce Also Reduced

The store closures form part of a broader restructuring programme approved by Starbucks’ board.The company has undertaken multiple rounds of corporate workforce reductions, including around 900 corporate job cuts, following the elimination of roughly 2,000 corporate roles in the previous year along with hundreds of vacant positions.

More than 200 employees were also dismissed in August after refusing relocation to Starbucks’ Nashville office, while another 300 corporate positions were eliminated following the closure of regional offices in Chicago, Atlanta, Dallas and Burbank, according to The Wall Street Journal.

Starbucks had previously estimated total restructuring expenses of approximately US$1 billion, with most of the costs linked to its North American operations. These expenses include employee separation benefits, store asset impairments and lease-related costs associated with closing locations before the expiry of their leases.

Focus On Cost Efficiency

The restructuring comes as Starbucks seeks to improve operational efficiency and profitability across its business. According to The Wall Street Journal, Niccol has set a target of reducing costs by US$2 billion before the end of fiscal 2028.As of late June, Starbucks operated 11,149 company-owned and company-operated stores across North America, around 300 fewer than a year earlier.

The company has also indicated that a significant share of future expansion will take place outside North America, while exploring smaller-format store concepts for the US market.

Technology Investment Continues

The Chennai GCC adds a technology and business capability layer to Starbucks’ global operations at a time when the company is simultaneously reassessing its physical retail and corporate footprint.

For India, the centre adds to the growing presence of global companies establishing GCCs to access technology and specialised talent. For Starbucks, the investment comes alongside efforts to reduce costs and rationalise operations in its largest retail markets.

data.title: India Tech Startups Raise $10.3 Bn In 9M 2026, Funding Rounds Fall 38%
data.description:
Funding rounds fell 38 per cent even as early-stage investments rose 27 per cent and six startups achieved unicorn status during the period

India’s technology startup ecosystem raised $10.3 billion in funding between January and September 2026, a 7 per cent increase year-on-year, even as the number of funding rounds declined sharply, according to a report by Tracxn Technologies Limited.

The report, which analyses equity funding, exits and unicorn activity between 1 January and 21 September 2026, recorded 1,134 funding rounds, down 38 per cent from the corresponding period last year. The data indicates a greater concentration of capital among a smaller number of companies, with larger transactions accounting for a significant share of overall funding.

Early-Stage Funding Gains

Early-stage funding rose 27 per cent to $4.2 billion during the period, while seed-stage funding declined 37 per cent to $698 million. Late-stage funding stood at $5.4 billion and remained largely unchanged.

The number of companies receiving funding for the first time fell 30 per cent to 338, while Series A and later rounds declined 23 per cent to 409.

At the same time, nearly 18 funding rounds exceeded $100 million, including a $1 billion private equity transaction, pointing to continued availability of significant capital for companies that meet investor expectations on growth and scale.

Enterprise Technology Leads

Enterprise Applications, FinTech and Enterprise Infrastructure were among the strongest-funded sectors during the first nine months of the year.Enterprise Applications attracted $3.5 billion, up 49 per cent year-on-year, while FinTech funding reached $2.2 billion, an increase of 13 per cent. Enterprise Infrastructure recorded the sharpest growth, with funding rising 436 per cent to $1.6 billion.

AI Infrastructure emerged as the most-funded theme, attracting $1.2 billion during the period. Digital Lending received $799 million, while Payments attracted $773 million.The sectoral distribution reflects continued investor interest in enterprise technology, financial technology and infrastructure supporting artificial intelligence deployments.

Six New Unicorns Created

India saw six new unicorns emerge during the first nine months of 2026, up from four during the same period in 2025.The latest cohort also reached the billion-dollar valuation threshold with lower average funding than startups that achieved unicorn status during the corresponding period last year.

The average funding raised before reaching unicorn status stood at $101 million in 2026, compared with $205 million in 2025. The average time taken to cross a $1 billion valuation after Series A also declined to 4.9 years from 6.6 years.

Funding Concentrates Further

The funding data presents a mixed picture for India’s startup ecosystem. Overall capital deployment increased, but the number of transactions, first-time funded companies and Series A-plus rounds declined.

At the same time, growth in early-stage funding, larger transactions and the emergence of six unicorns indicate that capital continues to be available for startups demonstrating growth and scale potential.The figures point to a funding environment in which the quantum of capital has remained resilient even as the pool of funded companies has narrowed.

data.title: Hospitality education faces the test of a new decade
data.description:
The Hospitality Education & Leadership Conversations, titled ‘Preparing Hospitality Leaders for a New Decade: Is Education Keeping Pace?’, brought together industry and academic leaders to discuss how hospitality education can evolve alongside the changing needs of the sector

With the conversations of Day 1 setting the tone for what lies ahead, the BW Hotelier Indian Hospitality Summit & Awards (IHA 2026) returned for its second day at the JW Marriott New Delhi Aerocity. The opening day brought together hospitality leaders, developers, investors, global brands and industry veterans, with discussions spanning growth, capital, development, leadership and the changing business of hospitality. Day 2 picked up where those conversations left off, bringing fresh voices and perspectives to the table.

The Hospitality Education & Leadership Conversations, titled ‘Preparing Hospitality Leaders for a New Decade: Is Education Keeping Pace?’, brought together industry and academic leaders to discuss how hospitality education can evolve alongside the changing needs of the sector.

The discussion was chaired by Kamal Kant Pant, Former Principal, IHM Pusa, New Delhi, and brought together Prabhat Verma, Chief People Officer, Indian Hotels Company Limited (IHCL), Mumbai; Raja Sadhukhan, Principal, IHM Kolkata; and Meenakshi Sumbly, Principal In-charge, IHM Pusa, New Delhi; Sangeetha Gandhi, VP, The Oberoi Centre of Learning and Development (OCLD); Meenakshi Sumbly, Principal In-charge, IHM Pusa, New Delhi; Smeetha Guha, Dean, Indian School of Hospitality.

Pant said, “The hospitality industry has been seeing significant investment, with people picking larger boxes, grander properties and an ever-increasing repertoire of services and facilities. But the question we need to ask is whether we have one of the most important ingredients required to run a hospitality establishment — the human power or human resources. As the industry continues to grow, we need to ensure that the talent and manpower required to support this expansion are keeping pace with the sector’s needs.”

Guha addressed, “The need for management and core skills is very important, and one of our philosophies is to focus on management skills. The feedback from our students is that they fit well into the hospitality sector, and the skill sets we have given them have made them more confident. It is not necessary that a good steward would make a good general manager.”

Sadhukhan said, “Hospitality is an emotional marketplace. A conscious leader with an abundance mindset can manifest excellence for guests and staff, and that is what we have been preparing the industry for. We are not just preparing students, but brand custodians.”

Sumbly, “The exposure given by IHM Pusa is something that cannot be gained from books. It is experiential learning that we are working on, and it is not just about culinary skills but also includes the small things, such as managing events, that prepare students for the realities of the hospitality industry.”

Gandhi said, “I think more than what is amiss, the generational shift that has happened is something that both education and industry need to be very mindful of. One gap that exists is preparing youngsters for the application of learning and not just learning. Today, information is available in the palm of our hands in microseconds, so the need is to be able to think on our feet and apply learning very quickly and swiftly. A learner’s ability to adapt to change is the need of the hour.”

Nagar

The session concluded with a stark call to action: closing the gap between classroom curricula and real-world operational demands is critical to sustaining India's hospitality boom. Educational leaders agreed that institutions must move quickly to equip graduates with practical digital capabilities, commercial acumen, and strong leadership skills alongside traditional service fundamentals.

The conversations will eventually give way to celebration as IHA 2026 heads into its Gala Awards evening. Bringing the two-day gathering to its culmination, BW Hotelier will recognise accomplished hoteliers and hospitality organisations across 20+ categories, acknowledging the people and businesses that have contributed to the sector’s growth and evolution.

data.title: Consumers stay strong, but a bear market could change that
data.description:
Key points:
  • Main US indexes modestly green; Dow out front, up ~0.6%
  • Tech leads S&P 500 sector gainers; energy weakest group
  • Euro STOXX 600 index up ~0.4%
  • Dollar, US crude, bitcoin all lower; gold gains
  • US 10-year Treasury yield rises to ~5.17%

CONSUMERS STAY STRONG, BUT A BEAR MARKET COULD CHANGE THAT

Despite high inflation and elevated fuel costs, Sonu Varghese, chief macro strategist at Carson Group, argues in a note out on Wednesday that the US consumer remains in surprisingly good shape.

His main point is that households are still spending rather than pulling back. Recent retail sales data showed solid spending not only on essentials but also on discretionary items such as restaurant meals. Varghese notes that dining out is often one of the first expenses consumers cut when budgets come under pressure. Instead, households appear willing to absorb higher prices while maintaining spending volumes.

The labor market is telling a similar story. Jobless claims remain historically low, layoffs are subdued and continuing claims suggest unemployed workers are finding jobs relatively quickly. Taken together, strong spending and a healthy labor market point to a consumer sector that continues to support economic growth.

Varghese also highlights the strength of household balance sheets. Debt levels relative to income remain well below pre-financial-crisis norms, while household net worth relative to income is at a record high. Unlike the period leading up to the housing bust, consumers are not borrowing aggressively to fund spending.

The caveat is that much of this strength is tied to rising asset prices, especially stocks. Equity holdings now account for a record share of household net worth, leaving consumers more exposed to market swings than in the past.

That leads to Varghese's bottom line: the biggest threat to the consumer is not excessive debt or a weakening labor market, but a sustained bear market. A prolonged decline in stock prices could erode household wealth, slow spending, weaken hiring and ultimately weigh on economic growth.

In short, consumers remain a key source of economic resilience. But with household wealth increasingly tied to the stock market, a prolonged bear market may now pose a bigger risk to the economy than rising debt levels.

data.title: Designing hotels for experience and long-term value
data.description:
The Design & Project Development Conversations, titled ‘Designing Hotels That Guests Remember and Owners Value’, brought together architects and design and project leaders to discuss the role of design in creating hotels that work for both guests and owners

With the conversations of Day 1 setting the tone for what lies ahead, the BW Hotelier Indian Hospitality Summit & Awards (IHA 2026) returned for its second day at the JW Marriott New Delhi Aerocity. The opening day brought together hospitality leaders, developers, investors, global brands and industry veterans, with discussions spanning growth, capital, development, leadership and the changing business of hospitality. Day 2 picked up from where those conversations left off, bringing a fresh set of voices and perspectives to the table.

As India’s hospitality sector continues to expand, hotel design and project development are increasingly being shaped by the need to balance guest experience with long-term asset value. The Design & Project Development Conversations, titled ‘Designing Hotels That Guests Remember and Owners Value’, brought together architects and design and project leaders to discuss the role of design in creating hotels that work for both guests and owners.

The discussion was chaired by Dikshu Kukreja, Managing Principal, CP Kukreja Architects (CPKA), and brought together Reema Diwan, VP - Design & Technical Services, India & South Asia, Accor; Senthil Kumar G, Design & Projects Director - Technical Services - India & Subcontinent, Hilton; Sahil Khan, VP & Head of Design and Planning, The Oberoi Group; Abhishek Singhal, VP - Projects & Technical Services, The Leela Palaces, Hotels and Resorts; and Anirban Dutta, Principal Architect & Interior Designer, Sbaspectra and Tejbeer Singh, Founder & Principal Architect, Expressionist.

Kukreja said, “The hotel is much more than an amalgamation of spaces. People often think about a hotel from the perspective of aesthetics, beauty or iconicity in a city, but it is really about bringing together all the different elements that make the hospitality experience work. Whether it is the guest spaces, back-of-the-house areas or engineering aspects, every element comes together. A hotel needs to be looked at from the eyes of all the different players who come into it, whether it is the owner, operator or guest. It is not just about the aesthetics of a hotel, but about understanding and bringing together all these different perspectives,”

Diwan addressed, “Design and technical services are not just about aesthetics, colour or how things are placed. It is about creating asset value, commercial sense and ROI. Every design decision should add value for the guest, operations or the asset. For economy brands, efficiency is critical, as every inch of space matters. India’s diversity also makes material selection important, considering wear and tear and how properties will age. Design is not about being expensive or inexpensive; it is about being relevant to the product, positioning, market and demography.”

Kumar said, “Hotel design is pretty straightforward: whether it is budget, mid-scale, upscale or luxury, we need to get the right product and design in place. The underlying principle remains the same across brands — the functional aspect of the room has to provide the utmost comfort to the guest. The level of layering, generosity of space and customisation may vary according to the brand and its positioning, but functionality remains fundamental. Fire safety and other essential systems are also an utmost priority, and we do not compromise on these aspects across segments.”

Khan explained, “Oberoi has been around for 90 years, and until now, we have always hovered around 30, 32 or 35 properties. Today, we are building and renovating the complete portfolio, with around 65 hotels under development. Even with this scale, our approach remains centred on the guest. We work from macro to micro, beginning with master planning, context and architecture, and then looking at how every space comes together, from the driveway and arrival court to the lobby. The guest journey has to be thought through as one contiguous experience, from the time a guest makes a reservation until they leave. That extends to the smallest details, including the location of a switch, the distance between a chair and table and the height of a table.”

Singhal said, “For us, the starting point is that a Leela hotel should unmistakably feel Leela. True Indian luxury is about expressing what is distinctive about India through a contemporary luxury lens, while creating a strong sense of place. The guest journey begins much before the room, from the arrival and common spaces to restaurants and wellness. Craftsmanship, materiality, art and attention to detail help express genuine Indian luxury. Ultimately, the true test of design is not only how beautiful the property looks, but how the guest feels — with warmth, comfort and a sense of being cared for.”

Dutta shared, “A hotel is not experienced just as a building; rather, it should be experienced as a sequence of cordial moments. As architects, our responsibility is to design and stitch those moments seamlessly together, from the arrival experience and transition from the road to the quality of light, materials and intricate details. Every small space in a hotel has an emotional impact, and I believe a hotel should be designed as a beautiful journey rather than just another floor plan. A memorable hotel is one where every user experience is collectively choreographed to make it effortless. While vibrant architecture gives a hotel its identity, these small sensory moments are what make it memorable and timeless.”

Singh said, “As an architect, I feel any product is relevant only if it is sustainable, lasting and relevant to its context. We try to bring regional aspects into our designs, whether it is incorporating the culture of Himachal or using materials that relate to a particular country or city. A good design does not need a high price; it needs a good thought. We can choose locally available products and materials, design around them and work out the costing. The idea is to create details that are relevant and lasting, rather than following fast fashion, while studying materials and spaces in depth to ensure the design remains sustainable and relevant.”

Wrapping up the session, the panel highlighted that a hotel's physical footprint directly dictates its long-term commercial success. By embedding intelligent, sustainable design principles right from the planning phase, hotel owners and brands can lower operational friction, enhance long-term asset value, and ensure properties remain competitive throughout India's hospitality growth decade.

The conversations will eventually give way to celebration as IHA 2026 heads into its Gala Awards evening. Bringing the two-day gathering to its culmination, BW Hotelier will recognise accomplished hoteliers and hospitality organisations across 20+ categories, acknowledging the people and businesses that have contributed to the sector’s growth and evolution.

data.title: Florida's Brightline railroad lines up $490 million for bankruptcy restructuring
data.description:
By Dietrich Knauth

Florida's Brightline commuter railroad said Friday that it has lined up $490 million in new financing to restructure some of its parent company debt, while leaving other bond debt untouched.

  • 17 Brightline affiliates filed for Chapter 11 in New Jersey late Thursday.

  • Brightline Trains Florida LLC, the train operating company, will remain outside of bankruptcy.

  • Brightline said the debt restructuring will not impact $2.2 billion in bond debt that was used to finance the company's rail construction.

  • Brightline operates a high-speed Miami-to-Orlando private rail line.

  • The debt restructuring will allow the rail company to re-invest in operations and capitalize on "real momentum," Brightline CEO Patrick Goddard said.

  • Ridership is up 14% from last year and revenue is up 17%, according to Brightline.

  • Bankruptcy petitions list over $1 billion in assets and over $1 billion in liabilities.

data.title: Iowa American Water Highlights the Role of Source Water Protection in Providing High-Quality Water
data.description:
DAVENPORT, Iowa, Sept. 25, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- In recognition of American Water Works Association's Annual Source Water Protection Week (September 27 to October 3), Iowa American Water is highlighting its commitment to providing customers with safe, clean, reliable water services.

"Protecting our source water is the first step in providing safe, clean, reliable drinking water," said Brad Nielsen, Iowa American Water President. "Keeping our rivers, lakes and groundwater free from pollution reduces potential risks that could negatively impact the water supply and keeps treatment costs down."

American Water's Source Water Protection Program provides a structured framework for assessing risks, engaging stakeholders and implementing proactive measures to safeguard drinking water supplies.

Iowa American Water's source water protection efforts include:

  • Robust monitoring systems and application of the most advanced technology, equipment and filtration processes.
  • Continued work with the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency and other state and local agencies to meet or surpass water quality standards and address emerging contaminants.
  • Constant collaboration with local emergency management and industry leaders to ensure emergency response plans are in place to minimize potential impacts to our water sources.
  • Working with water experts and utilities across the country to share ideas and best practices to protect drinking water in Iowa.

One example of source water protection in action is how Iowa American Water prepares for and responds to harmful algae blooms. These blooms can develop seasonally in rivers and may affect water quality if they are not addressed. Although they have historically been uncommon in the Mississippi River, Iowa American Water has identified several in recent years through routine monitoring at its Davenport water treatment plant. Because trained employees and response plans are already in place, the company can quickly adjust treatment as needed and continue providing customers with safe, high-quality water.

Additionally, American Water conducts nearly 1 million tests and measurements each year at the company's state-of-the-art research laboratories.

"Source water protection is a year-round effort that requires community collaboration," said Ted Kratschmer, Iowa American Water Source Water Protection Program Manager. "Source water protection at Iowa American Water is not just a plan sitting on a shelf. We take a proactive approach, engaging in regional efforts to help protect and improve our drinking water sources; however, we all play a role in safeguarding our water."

During Source Water Protection Week, Iowa American Water is encouraging individuals to take the following actions and incorporate them into their year-round practices:

  • Plant landscaping around homes or businesses with more permeable surfaces, such as mulch, that allow water to soak into the ground.
  • Do not over-apply chemicals to plants and avoid application immediately before it rains. 
  • Keep litter, pet waste and yard waste out of streets and storm drains. Pet waste contains bacteria that can find its way into waterways through runoff. 
  • Select non-toxic or less toxic alternatives to typical household products, such as cleaning agents. 
  • Dispose of pharmaceuticals by taking them to collection sites, where available. Don't flush them down the toilet! 
  • Use hazardous waste collection sites and services to dispose of items such as chemicals, paints, motor oil and batteries. Report any hazardous material spills, illegal dumping or suspicious activity to local or state authorities. 

Learn more about how water is treated and how it makes it to your tap here.

Read more about how the company strengthens operational readiness, uses technology to stay ahead of water quality challenges, builds stronger communities through partnership and prepares for emerging issues through recent case studies in states across our service areas here.

About American Water

American Water () is the largest regulated water and wastewater utility company in the United States. With a history dating back to 1886 and celebrating 140 years in 2026, We Keep Life Flowing® by providing safe, clean, reliable and affordable drinking water and wastewater services to approximately 14 million people with regulated operations in 14 states and on 19 military installations. American Water's approximately 7,000 talented professionals leverage their significant expertise and the company's national size and scale to achieve excellent outcomes for the benefit of customers, employees, investors and other stakeholders.

For more information, visit amwater.com and join American Water on LinkedIn, Facebook, X and Instagram.

About Iowa American WaterIowa American Water, a subsidiary of American Water, is the largest regulated water utility in the state with approximately 90 dedicated employees working to provide safe, clean, reliable and affordable water and wastewater services to approximately 225,000 people.

SOURCE American Water
